questions.question: When was the Bardoli Movement launched?
questions.solution:
• Bardoli Satyagraha: 1928
  • Leadership: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led this movement against the 22% tax increase imposed by the British in Gujarat.

questions.question: In which year was Battle of Peshawar fought between Raja Jayapal and Mahmud Ghazni?
questions.solution:
• Peshawar 1001: 1001
  • Invasion: This victory allowed Mahmud of Ghazni to open the gateway to the Indian plains for his subsequent raids.

questions.question: Which act was passed by the British Government of India to introduce Provincial Autonomy?
questions.solution:
• 1935 Act: Government of India Act of 1935
  • Detail: This act replaced 'Dyarchy' with Provincial Autonomy and paved the way for the federal structure of modern India.

questions.question: Who wrote the "Harshacharita", a biography of Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
• Harshacharita: Banabhatta
  • History: Banabhatta was the court poet of King Harshavardhana and his work is the earliest surviving royal biography in Sanskrit.

questions.question: When was the Lucknow Pact signed by All India Muslim League and Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
• Lucknow Pact: 1916
  • Unity: For the first time, the Congress and the Muslim League presented joint constitutional demands to the British government.

questions.question: Under ______ (Governor General from 1813 to 1823) a new policy of “paramountcy” was initiated. Now the Company claimed that its authority was paramount or supreme, hence its power was greater than that of Indian states.
questions.solution:
• Policy of Paramountcy: Lord Hastings
  • Theory: Under Lord Hastings, the British asserted that their power was supreme over all Indian princely states.

questions.question: Buddha meditated for days on end under a peepal tree at ______, where he attained enlightenment.
questions.solution:
• Bodh Gaya: Bodh Gaya
  • Buddhism: Siddhartha Gautama attained Nirvana here at the age of 35, becoming the Buddha (the Awakened One).

questions.question: The nineteenth century saw the golden age of Kathak under the patronage of ____________, the last Nawab of Oudh.
questions.solution:
• Kathak Patron: Wajid Ali Shah
  • Fact: The Nawab was himself a trained dancer and musician, composing many pieces under the pen name 'Akhtarpiya'.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army?
I. Sawar - Men on horses
II. Musket - A heavy gun used by infantry soldiers
questions.solution:
• Army Terms: Both I and II
  • Company Military: Sawars (cavalry) and Musketeers (infantry with heavy guns) formed the core of the Company's disciplined professional force.

questions.question: Who among the following was famously known as the "The parrot of India"?
questions.solution:
• Parrot of India: Amir Khusro
  • Detail: A Sufi musician and poet, Tuti-e-Hind (Amir Khusro) is credited with inventing the Sitar and the Qawwali musical style.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when in ______ a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura.
questions.solution:
• Chauri Chaura: February 1922
  • Impact: Gandhi halted the movement because he believed the Indian people were not yet ready for a purely non-violent struggle.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote a history of Akbar’s reign titled Akbar Nama?
questions.solution:
• Akbar Nama: Abul Fazl
  • Literature: This monumental work is divided into three volumes, the third being the famous Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital under the rule of Tipu Sultan?
questions.solution:
• Tipu's Capital: Seringapatam
  • History: The capital fell in 1799 during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, where Tipu Sultan died defending the city.

questions.question: ______ was the capital city of the Vijaynagar Empire.
questions.solution:
• Vijayanagar Capital: Hampi
  • Fact: Hampi was one of the largest and richest cities in the world in the 15th century, now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.question: In ______, a Subsidiary Alliance system was imposed on Awadh by the British.
questions.solution:
• Awadh Alliance: 1801
  • Terms: The Nawab was forced to disband his army and cede half of his territory (Rohilkhand and the Doab) to the British.

questions.question: __________ was the first governor-general of Bengal.
questions.solution:
• First GG of Bengal: Warren Hastings
  • 1773: He was appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773, centralizing the administration of the three presidencies.

questions.question: Who among the following was a ruler of Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Shunga Ruler: Pushyamitra
  • History: Pushyamitra Shunga was the commander-in-chief of the last Maurya king, whom he assassinated to start his own dynasty.

questions.question: Before the Partition of Bengal in 1905, Bengal was the biggest province of British India. It consisted of parts of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
• Greater Bengal: Bihar and Orissa
  • Context: In 1905, Bengal was a massive administrative unit; its partition sparked the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a component of Lion Capital at Sarnath, India?
questions.solution:
• Lion Capital: Carved cow representing South direction
  • Correction: The base of the capital features a bull (West), a horse (South), an elephant (East), and a lion (North). There is no cow.

questions.question: When was the Champaran Agrarian Act passed?
questions.solution:
• Champaran Act: 1918
  • Outcome: This act abolished the Tinkathia system and offered relief to the oppressed indigo farmers.

questions.question: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country
questions.solution:
• Lahore Resolution: 1940
  • Politics: Often called the 'Pakistan Resolution,' it marked the formal demand for separate sovereign states for Muslims.

questions.question: The city of Fatehpur Sikri was built by ______.
questions.solution:
• Fatehpur Sikri: Akbar
  • Architecture: Akbar built this 'City of Victory' to honor the Sufi saint Salim Chishti, who predicted the birth of his son.

questions.question: When did Indigo revolt, a peasant movement, start in India?
questions.solution:
• Indigo Revolt: 1859
  • Fact: Started in Nadia, Bengal, this was a highly organized peasant resistance where farmers refused to grow indigo for European planters.

questions.question: How many Vedas are there in Indian literature of classical Hinduism?
questions.solution:
• Four Vedas: Four
  • List: The four Vedas are the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.

questions.question: In ______, Ambedkar started a temple entry movement, in which his Mahar caste followers participated.
questions.solution:
• Temple Entry: 1927
  • Social Justice: This movement was a significant step by Dr. Ambedkar to assert the human rights of Dalits and challenge untouchability.
